newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Volvo strike halts Brazil production.
newsitem.headline: Volvo strike halts Brazil production.

text.p: A two-day old strike by hundreds of Volvo AB workers has halted production at the company's bus and truck plant in Brazil's Parana state, a Volvo spokesman said.
"This strike has stopped our production line," said Walter Viapiana, a spokesman for Volvo's local unit.
He added that the strike over salary adjustments has prevented the firm from assembling 30 heavy trucks and 14 buses.
Brazil is Volvo's second and fourth largest market for buses and heavy trucks, respectively, he said.

Volvo workers were scheduled to return to work on Jan 7 after a 24-day yearend break but decided to go on strike on Tuesday to demand wage increases of 10 percent. Volvo was offering wage hikes of seven percent and nine percent, Viapiana said.
The company said it produced roughly 3,500 heavy trucks and 1,100 buses in Brazil last year.
